Question: The signal \( x(t) \) undergoes ideal sampling, resulting in the sampled signal \( x_s(t) = x(t) \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} \delta\left(t - nT_s\right) \) (where \( n \) is an integer). The spectrum of the sampled signal is shown in the <image> with no aliasing. Determine the sampling interval \( T_s \).

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled X_s(ω), and the horizontal axis is angular frequency ω. After sampling, the spectrum is shown as a series of identical triangular spectrum replicas; the three visible main replicas are centered at −4π, 0, and +4π respectively, the central replica is roughly from −π to +π, and the left and right replicas do not overlap with the central replica. Reasoning: ideal sampling x_s(t)=x(t)Σδ(t−nT_s) produces periodically repeated spectrum replicas in the frequency domain, and the center spacing between adjacent replicas is the sampling angular frequency ω_s. From the figure, the adjacent center spacing is 4π, so ω_s=4π. The sampling angular frequency and sampling interval satisfy ω_s=2π/T_s, so T_s=2π/ω_s=2π/(4π)=0.5. Expressed to one decimal place, it is 0.5.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the sampled spectrum X_s(ω) shows identical triangular replicas centered at -4π, 0, and +4π, with no overlap. From the text, x_s(t)=x(t)Σδ(t-nT_s), so ideal sampling creates frequency-domain replicas spaced by ω_s. Use the visual spacing between adjacent replica centers, ω_s=4π. Then compute T_s=2π/ω_s=2π/(4π)=0.5 and report to one decimal place.
